transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-14 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~46 minutes
Attendees: Maria Chen (Redwood AE), Ethan Park (Redwood SE), Rajiv Malhotra (CTO - NimbusPay), Diana Lopez (Head of ML), Samir Patel (Infra Lead)
Recording id: ff-20260914-nimbuspay-01

Summary: (auto) Quick discovery on latency & throughput requirements; got detailed constraints on p95 latency, concurrency patterns, streaming expectations and security/compliance needs.

[00:00] Maria Chen: hey everyone thanks for joining, this is Maria from Redwood AE, with Ethan our SE. how's it going?
[00:12] Rajiv Malhotra: good thanks, we've been looking at Redwood cuz we need something predictable for our payments flows, low latency for auth chat, and also tight security.
[00:22] Ethan Park: great, quick agenda — understand your goals (p95 targets, concurrency), current infra, streaming needs, then map hosted/dedicated/private tradeoffs.
[00:33] Diana Lopez: sounds good. I'll try to focus on the ML perf side — our models are 13B and a couple of tuned 33B variants. mostly short responses but with occasional longer contexts.
[00:45] Samir Patel: and infra concerns — we need VPC options and KMS integration because of regs.

[01:05] Maria Chen: perfect. first, what are your p95 targets and typical concurrency? like what's acceptable for auth path vs async batch?
[01:16] Rajiv Malhotra: for the auth path we need p95 under 200ms for responses under ~60 tokens. our broad target is 150-200ms p95 for short form responses. For streaming chat we want initial token out under 150ms and steady-state token rate so the user sees smooth typing — ideally >= 25-50 tokens/sec.
[01:40] Ethan Park: okay that's helpful. rough QPS? peak concurrent requests?
[01:46] Diana Lopez: during peak we see 600 concurrent sessions for auth checks, but per-session requests are small; for chat it's smaller concurrency, maybe 120 concurrent streams but with higher token/sec sustained bursts.
[02:05] Maria Chen: so two workloads — high-concurrency short inference and lower-concurrency streaming with throughput requirements. good.

[02:20] Rajiv Malhotra: what's the difference if we choose Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private for these SLOs? we care about predictability as much as median.
[02:33] Ethan Park: short answer: Hosted is fastest to get started and cost-effective but multi-tenant noise can vary p95; Dedicated gives you isolated GPU pools and more predictable p95 and throughput; Private (VPC/on-prem) gives the tightest network controls and no egress to public plane but requires more ops. For your 150-200ms p95 on short responses, dedicated or a very optimized hosted profile with pinned models usually hit that.
[02:58] Samir Patel: when you say pinned models on Hosted, does that reserve capacity? we don't want noisy neighbors causing p95 spikes.
[03:07] Ethan Park: yes — we offer reserved capacity overlays for hosted that pin some instances to your account (we call that reserved or Dedicated overlay), but pure Dedicated gives SLA-backed isolation. We can show benchmarks.

[03:28] Diana Lopez: about models — we're running quantized 13B (int8) and a 33B q4_k8-ish variant. what's your typical token/sec on those?
[03:38] Ethan Park: rough numbers — on H100-class hardware with optimized kernels, you can see ~2k-6k tokens/sec for 13B depending on batching and sequence length; 33B drops to ~700-2k tokens/sec. But aware these vary by quantization and kernel selection. We'll run your exact model to give apples-to-apples.
[04:05] Rajiv Malhotra: those are ballpark; our ask is p95 under 200ms for short prompts. Do you have data for p95 at different concurrency levels?
[04:16] Ethan Park: yes; typically we report p50/p95/p99 for synthetic bench. p95 at low concurrency (1-10) for 13B can be ~40-80ms on H100, but at high concurrency and without batching it can climb. That's where our batching and prefix/KV cache helps. We'll run benchmarks at 600 concurrent short requests to mimic your auth path — that will show realistic p95.

[04:52] Maria Chen: also streaming — you mentioned token/sec; for chat we need stable streaming with low jitter. Redwood supports streaming with chunked tokens and can prioritize steady-state streaming vs latency. any caveats there?
[05:08] Ethan Park: streaming introduces two pieces — initial generation latency and sustained token throughput. For initial token you want warm KV cache and minimized kernel setup. For sustained, we measured 25-100 tokens/sec depending on model/hardware. We'll aim to validate your 25-50 tokens/sec target. Also we can trade off quantization profiles to improve token/sec.

[05:36] Rajiv Malhotra: network hop — if we go Private VPC, how much extra added latency does the control plane add, and do we have to manage the model updates?
[05:48] Ethan Park: Private VPC keeps the data plane inside your network and control plane can be in a customer-managed cluster or our control plane with private connectors. Typically data path latency depends on co-location; for on-prem endpoints it can actually reduce latency. Model rollouts can be controlled by you — we provide orchestration hooks.

[06:10] Diana Lopez: we also care about cold starts — can you maintain KV cache warm for certain sessions? we have a lot of repetitive prefixes in auth flows.
[06:20] Ethan Park: yes — you can configure sticky routing / session pinning and pre-warm KV cache. Our runtime supports prefix caching and reuse to shave tens to hundreds of ms on repeated flows.

[06:40] Samir Patel: security check: KMS/HSM integration, SAML SSO, audit logs, retention controls — standard enterprise needs.
[06:50] Maria Chen: we have those — we support KMS integrations, customer-managed keys in Private, SAML/SSO and detailed audit logs. we'll share the SOC2 docs.

[07:05] Rajiv Malhotra: what's the plan for running the benchmark? we can provide a sample trace.
[07:12] Ethan Park: ideal is you provide sample traces and typical prompt distributions (tokens per request, seq lengths), then we'll run three profiles: hosted standard, hosted reserved (pinned), and dedicated pool. We'll measure p50/p95/p99 and token/sec streaming and surface tail latencies.

[07:34] Diana Lopez: we'll share the traces. our prompts are typically 20-60 tokens for auth and for chat 200-800 context with ~30-80 token outputs.

[07:50] Maria Chen: good. one engineering question — what's your approach for batching? we don't want increased p95 because of batching latency.
[07:58] Ethan Park: Redwood's runtime uses adaptive batching with latency SLOs. you can set a per-route latency target (p95 threshold) and the runtime will balance batching vs latency. For the auth route we would set a tight per-request SLO to favor lower latency and smaller batches; for batch/throughput routes, we allow larger batching to improve token efficiency.

[08:26] Rajiv Malhotra: and cost? any ballpark delta between hosted pinned and dedicated?
[08:33] Maria Chen: dedicated is typically higher fixed cost but gives better predictability and lower per-token jitter; hosted pinned is lower fixed, pay-as-you-go. we'll send typical numbers in the pricing proposal.

[08:50] Samir Patel: any recommendations on hardware — A10 vs H100 for our use case?
[08:56] Ethan Park: for high-concurrency short requests A10-like instances can be cost-effective; for low-latency p95 and high token/sec streaming H100 (or equivalent) offers headroom. Also quantization profiles change the hardware ROI; for 13B int8 you get great density. We'll include recommended configs in the bench report.

[09:22] Diana Lopez: curious — do you support multi-model fallbacks? if H100 capacity is constrained, we might want fallback to a smaller quantized model.
[09:31] Ethan Park: yes, smart routing and model variant fallbacks are supported — policy-based routing by latency/cost/region, automatic fallback to a compatible variant when capacity constrained.

[09:45] Maria Chen: ok let's talk concrete benchmarks — Ethan, can you commit to running p95 token/sec tests for: 13B int8 at 600 concurrent short requests, and 33B q4 at 120 concurrent streaming sessions at target 30 tokens/sec?
[10:00] Ethan Park: yes we'll do: 1) 13B int8 @ 600 conc short prompts (20-60 tokens) measure p50/p95/p99; 2) 33B q4 @ 120 streams measure initial token latency + sustained tokens/sec and jitter; 3) one hosted pinned vs dedicated comparison. We'll push results in a spreadsheet.

[10:20] Rajiv Malhotra: timeline?
[10:22] Ethan Park: aim to run bench and share by 2026-09-21. Maria will follow up with proposal by 9/17.

[10:30] (brief cross-talk) Speaker 3: uh sorry one sec, connection lag.

[12:00] Diana Lopez: a couple of gotchas we saw with providers — p95 spikes when KV cache eviction happens, and when sequence length variability causes kernel re-selection. can you control or mitigate?
[12:15] Ethan Park: yes, we monitor kernel re-selection and proactively pin kernel sets for workload profiles; prefix caching helps a lot. Also we can configure cache eviction policies and warm strategies. We'll document these in the bench report.

[13:00] Samir Patel: SLO-wise, do you offer alerts if p95 crosses threshold?
[13:07] Maria Chen: yes our Console has per-route SLO monitoring and alerting, with tracing hooks. We can wire alerts to PagerDuty/Jira.

[13:25] Rajiv Malhotra: on data residency — some of our auth data must stay in EU. do you support region pinning?
[13:33] Ethan Park: yes region pinning is standard. for private deployments you can keep everything in-region and use customer-managed control planes.

[14:00] Diana Lopez: about metrics — we need token-level cost and latency breakdowns to feed into our cost model.
[14:08] Maria Chen: Redwood Console shows token-level cost, per-model latency histograms, and trace-level breakdowns. we'll include screenshots.

[14:30] Rajiv Malhotra: okay let's recap the acceptance criteria: p95 <= 200ms short auth; streaming initial token <150ms and sustained 25-50 tokens/sec with low jitter; isolated capacity for predictable p95; KMS, SAML, audit logs and regional residency.
[14:52] Maria Chen: yep that's what we'll validate. next steps: 1) NimbusPay to share sample request traces and SLO doc, 2) Redwood SE to run benchmarks and share spreadsheet by 9/21, 3) AE to send pricing/dedicated proposal by 9/17, 4) schedule deep technical bench session week of 9/21.

[15:10] Rajiv Malhotra: sounds good. one more question — if results show we miss p95 on hosted pinned, what's the rollback path?
[15:18] Ethan Park: we have automatic fallback policies and can recommend Dedicated pool sizing; if needed we can do canary deployments and rollback model variants. The engineering team will also work with you to tune caching and routing.

[15:38] Diana Lopez: for the bench, we'll provide prompts and a small sample payload generator. any preferences on load generator?
[15:45] Ethan Park: prefer k6 or locust; whatever you use is fine — we'll take your traces and run them through our harness for parity.

[16:00] Maria Chen: I'll attach a secure link to the SOC2 pack and the security questionnaire.
[16:06] Samir Patel: and please include info on KMS, HSM, and customer key lifecycle for Private deployment.

[16:22] Rajiv Malhotra: are you offering trial credits or pilot?
[16:26] Maria Chen: yes we have pilot credits and can spin up a short dedicated pilot pool for 2-4 weeks to validate p95 and streaming. I'll include pilot terms in the proposal.

[16:40] Diana Lopez: perfect. anything on function calling or structured outputs we should worry about? our responses are JSON-ish but small.
[16:49] Ethan Park: supported — function/tool calling and structured output are in the response layer and don't materially change token/sec, though structured parsing can add minimal overhead. We'll validate with your sample.

[17:05] Maria Chen: cool, if there are no other questions we'll recap actions and close out.
[17:12] Rajiv Malhotra: no further from me. thanks everyone.
[17:18] Diana Lopez: thanks, appreciate it.
[17:22] Maria Chen: thanks all, we'll follow up with links and timeline.
